hero.headline: Build, simulate, and fly drones — all in one IDE
hero.subheadline: Assemble quadcopters from real market components, wire them together, write flight code, run physics simulations, and export your build — before touching hardware.
hero.buildDescription: Browse the full catalog of motors, ESCs, flight controllers, frames, batteries, and cameras. Drag components onto the 3D canvas, wire them together, and see your drone take shape in real time.
hero.statsDescription: See estimated flight time, thrust-to-weight ratio, total power draw, and component weight breakdown — all calculated automatically as you build. Know your drone's limits before it ever leaves the ground.
hero.simDescription: Run your build through a full physics simulation. Test hover stability, throttle response, and crash scenarios in a safe virtual environment. Tune PID values and see the effect instantly.
hero.exportTitle: Export your build, ready to order
hero.exportDescription: Generate a complete parts list with affiliate links, wiring diagrams, and assembly instructions. Share your build with the community or order everything in one click.
hero.badge: Drone Application by Insai — v1.0 Available Now
hero.wireDescription: Connect pads between ESCs, flight controllers, motors, and cameras with an intuitive visual wiring tool. See exactly which pin connects where — no more guessing from datasheets.
hero.codeDescription: Program your quadcopter with Scratch-style block code. Define flight behaviors, autonomous routines, and failsafe logic — then test it all in the simulator before uploading.
hero.featuresHeading: Everything you need to build quadcopters
hero.featuresSubheading: From component selection to flight code — one integrated development environment.
hero.ideSubheading: See the full IDE in action — build, wire, code, and simulate in a single window.
hero.ctaHeading: Ready to build your first quadcopter?
hero.ctaSubheading: Download the trial IDE and start assembling with real components. Upgrade to a plan for the full version with simulation, export, and block code.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions about Drone Application by Insai.
faq.buildText: Assemble drones from real components and validate compatibility before buying hardware.
faq.codeText: Prototype flight behaviors with block code inside the simulator workflow.
faq.downloadText: Use the desktop app on Windows, macOS, or Linux with trial and paid plan options.
faq.sidebarText: The simulator is designed as a VS Code-style drone IDE: build, wire, code, simulate, then export.
faq.q1: What is Drone Application by Insai?
faq.a1: It is a desktop IDE for building quadcopters using real market components. You can assemble drones via drag-and-drop, wire components together, write flight code, simulate physics, view performance stats, and export your build as a parts list.
faq.a2: Windows, macOS, and Linux. Download the trial or full version from the Downloads page.
faq.a3: Yes, the trial version is free to download. It includes limited features so you can evaluate the IDE before purchasing a plan.
faq.q4: What do I get with a paid plan?
faq.a4: Full access to all components, simulation engine, block code editor, export functionality, and priority support. See the Pricing page for plan details.
faq.q5: Can I use real drone components?
faq.a5: Yes. The component catalog includes real products available on the market — motors, ESCs, flight controllers, frames, batteries, and cameras from brands like iFlight, T-Motor, SpeedyBee, and more.
faq.q6: What kind of code can I write?
faq.a6: You can use Scratch-style block code for advanced flight behaviors, autonomous routines, and failsafe logic. Test everything in the simulator before uploading to hardware.
faq.q7: Does the simulation use real physics?
faq.a7: Yes. The physics engine models thrust, drag, gravity, motor response curves, and PID control. You can tune PID values and see the effect in real time.
faq.a8: Yes. Export generates a complete parts list with purchase links, wiring diagrams, and step-by-step assembly instructions. Share with the community or order components directly.
